title: Pulmonary Embolism: Pretest Probability and Imaging
subject: Medicine
preview: Pulmonary embolism may cause dyspnea, pleuritic pain, tachycardia, syncope or hypoxemia; presentations vary.
quickRevision: Pulmonary embolism may cause dyspnea, pleuritic pain, tachycardia, syncope or hypoxemia; presentations vary.
CT pulmonary angiography is a common diagnostic imaging method when suitable; other pathways may be needed with contraindications.
Hemodynamic instability changes urgency and specialist treatment decisions.

sections.title: Clinical syndrome and red flags
points: Pulmonary embolism may cause dyspnea, pleuritic pain, tachycardia, syncope or hypoxemia; presentations vary.
A validated pretest probability approach guides whether D-dimer or imaging is appropriate.

sections.title: Exam trap — avoid this mistake
points: A negative D-dimer is not a universal rule-out in high-pretest-probability presentations.
